correction: Every head must stay attached to a visible neck and shoulders that run off the edge of the panel. No head may float free in the sky, and no neck may end in a cut, torn or jagged edge. Arrange the three men as a ring around the rim of the frame, all seen from directly below, foreshortened, and leaning over the viewer. The Fisherman leans in from the LEFT edge: his broad shoulders and upper chest run off the left border, and the white cotton cloth lies on his LEFT shoulder. Because he faces down at the viewer, that cloth shows on the viewer's RIGHT side of his neck. The Young Fisherman leans in from the TOP edge: his neck, both shoulders and the top of a faded blue sleeveless vest extend up and out of the top border, drawn foreshortened. The Wary Fisherman sits at the RIGHT edge, leaning in least, his head and shoulders turned partly away toward the right border, with the coiled net on his shoulder. Keep all three faces exactly as they are now: the grizzled leader with strong white teeth, the slim young man with the cloth headband and thin black beard, and the gaunt elder with the long grey-streaked beard. Keep the grey sky of stale rice water and the open patch of sky in the centre-bottom for the single caption.
issues: v01 (the only candidate) fails on anatomy. The Young Fisherman's head floats alone in the middle of the sky.
